data.component: WAN NIC (vtnet0, VirtIO) on the firewall - driver queue hang
data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver has hung: dmesg shows repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP cycles and sends fail with "No buffer space available", so the WAN path is dead even though the interface is UP, the DHCP lease is valid, and the ISP modem reports OPERATIONAL.
evidence: dmesg -a: three 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' entries interleaved with link DOWN/UP cycles - the transmit queue stops progressing and the link resets each time.
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 (ISP gateway): 'sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss; same for 1.1.1.1 - packets fail to leave the firewall itself.
netstat -i: vtnet0 shows Oerrs=48211 transmit errors while LAN vtnet1 has 0 - errors are confined to the WAN NIC.
arp -a -n: entry for default gateway 198.51.100.1 is '(incomplete)' despite route 'default 198.51.100.1 UGS vtnet0'.
ping -c 3 10.20.0.9 (LAN host): 0% loss - the network stack works; only traffic via vtnet0 fails.

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json and tail events.jsonl: ~12 WAN reloads since outage_start 02:01, all rc=0, connectivity never returned; at 03:30 watchdog logged action=none reason=reload_cap (12/12).
tail modem-events.jsonl / modem-metrics.jsonl: modem rebooted 02:28 after a T3 timeout and now reports OPERATIONAL with min_snr 37.7 dB - the ISP side is healthy.
cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0: lease 198.51.100.27 valid until 2026/3/6 - WAN/DHCP configuration is not the fault.
data.recommendation: The hang is in the firewall's own WAN NIC driver, below where DHCP renewal or the modem could help; the watchdog's twelve wan_reload cycles (rc=0) never restored connectivity, so another wan_reload will not clear a stuck virtio queue. The appropriate fix is a reboot of gw.lan (firewall_reboot, about 4 minutes down), which resets the driver. The maintainer is away tonight, so flag this for their approval as urgently as possible; until the box is reset the internet will stay down. Afterwards, consider making the watchdog escalate to a full host reset once its reload cap is hit instead of giving up.
